other_issues: Patch review, window sizing: the window is resized only when a gap exceeds the current window (`if (gap <= win) {}`), so it never shrinks inside a burst. It is not 'twice the last gap': it is max(2*gap, 10) capped at 50, and it stays put until a gap of 50 us or more sets it to 0. The gap is measured by the watcher, from the timestamp after the previous serve to the next detection, so it includes the watcher's own sleep delay. That can keep a closed window closed. WIN_MAX2 can be overridden through the environment, but no .env file sets it (checked), and all AC2 .env files have V2=1 while no AC .env file does.
Patch review, cap removal: exactly as described (`!V2 && t - hot_since > EPISODE_CAP`). The risky case for uncapped polling (a steady stream of gaps of 10-50 us) is not in the matrix.

Patch review, latch: V2 latches when a hit comes within HIT_WINDOW=1 s of the previous hit (last_hit), and notes do not reset it, as claimed. A start-up hit plus any real unnoted launch within 1 s will latch. Unlatch: evidence is recorded when a request is served while unseen, the cached `inflight` is false and generation()==seen_gen; the latch comes off after 1 s without evidence. `inflight` is refreshed only every 1 ms or more, so the check is approximate. In V2 the unlatch check runs only on calls where no new generation was seen. For an app that uses graphs and goes idle for more than 1 s, this rule would unlatch and then need two hits to latch again (an extra 1 ms backstop wait); this was not tested.

Patch review, the AC path with V2 off: unchanged apart from the diagnostics (t_gen_seen and t_idle bookkeeping, plus an extra any_running() call on hits). The agent library was rebuilt at 13:24:20 (src matches .ctl plus the patch byte for byte) and spin3 at 13:27:33 with the graph modes. So 'AC = AC of earlier rounds' and 'victim built as before' hold for the code, not for the binaries; compare numbers with earlier rounds with care.

summarize.py reads the max temperature only from the before/after .env snapshots. It drops only the first latency value, but graph cells have two warm-up calls (a plain one and one through the graph), so one warm-up call stays in each graph cell's latency set. It pools calls over 1 ms across rounds, so a single disturbed run can set the pooled share and the max (as in c02 AC2).

The machine was not quiet during r2: RAM ranged from 2.0 to 3.7 GB between runs, and there was outside CPU load from 13:40:47 to 13:42:15. Load cells (c01, c05, c10, c15, c17, c22, c24, c28) have no tegrastats, so disturbances in them cannot be detected; the only sign is a P load rate that is off, as in r2 c01_P.

For each set, 'minus P' uses a single P run per round, run one after the other rather than at the same time. Under load this baseline varies by about ±0.03 cores (r2 c24 AC2 comes out at -0.000), so CPU differences under 0.03 in load cells are within noise.
